question.text: The Vindhya Event-Driven Fund (Cat III AIF) has a target corpus of INR 300 crore. What is the MINIMUM sponsor commitment the manager must make to comply with SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: INR 5 crore (2.5% capped at INR 5 cr)
INR 10 crore (5% of INR 300 cr = INR 15 cr, capped at INR 10 cr)
INR 15 crore (5% of INR 300 cr, no cap)

explanation.text: The Logic: Cat III sponsor commit = 5% of corpus or INR 10 cr, whichever is LOWER. 5% of 300 cr = INR 15 cr. Lower of (INR 15 cr, INR 10 cr) = INR 10 cr. Sponsor must commit INR 10 cr. The Trap: Option A applies Cat I/II rule (2.5% / INR 5 cr) — the swap trap. Option B drops the cap. Option D forgets the INR 10 cr cap. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D tests Cat I/II's 2.5%/INR 5 cr; XIX-E tests Cat III's 5%/INR 10 cr. Memorise the split. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a INR 300 cr Cat III, sponsor's INR 10 cr is 3.33% of corpus. Whether you commit more (say 5%) for marketing optics is a governance call — at a minimum, meet the regulatory floor.
